description: V0.3-12 Desktop Project Open Foundation, executed as the first real AGENT-02 native pilot: 1 Main Agent + 3 native Tianshu workers on a SHARED worktree, pairwise C0. Re-issued at revision 2 with execution_mode=native-shared and the delivery coordinates each task actually had; the originals are preserved in git history at 8522c0f.

tasks.title: Desktop Runtime project read-model client
tasks.objective: Implement inspectProject(projectPath) in the desktop Runtime HTTP boundary: it calls GET /project/inspect?project_path=... and returns a typed Desktop read model { projectId, displayName, schemaVersion, createdAt, updatedAt }, mapping the Runtime's snake_case JSON onto camelCase only inside this boundary. projectPath is an explicit parameter on every call; there is no global current project, and the path is never normalised, resolved, lower-cased or rewritten - it is encoded as the project_path query parameter with URLSearchParams (or an equivalent safe query encoding) and forwarded verbatim. A successful response is validated field by field and a fresh object is built from exactly the declared fields - never cast. Failures are distinguished into three typed classes: a structured Runtime API error (the shared five-field envelope code / message / details / recoverable / source is preserved intact), a transport error, and a contract error (a 2xx payload the contract does not describe). No diagnostic may echo projectPath, the raw response body or an internal URL.
tasks.scope: The new desktop Runtime project client module and its vitest suite.
non_goals: Re-implementing the Runtime project domain - ProjectService stays the only project authority
Changing the Runtime HTTP contract or any module under runtime/
Any UI, project picker, recent-projects list or global current-project state
Any Rust, Tauri IPC or orchestration change
acceptance_criteria: inspectProject(projectPath) requests GET /project/inspect with project_path encoded by URLSearchParams, and a non-empty path reaches the query string byte for byte
A well-formed success payload is projected onto { projectId, displayName, schemaVersion, createdAt, updatedAt } with no extra field and no cast
A malformed success payload - missing field, wrong field type, non-object, array - is refused as a contract error and produces no read model
A structured Runtime failure keeps code / message / details / recoverable / source intact and is a Runtime API error, not a transport error
A transport failure and an uninterpretable failure response are transport errors
No error message or error field contains projectPath, the response body or the request URL

tasks.title: Native project directory selection bridge
tasks.objective: Add one native Tauri command, select_project_directory, that opens the OS directory dialog in Rust, lets the user choose a directory, and returns the chosen directory path (Ok(Some(path)) on selection, Ok(None) when the dialog is dismissed). The command accepts ZERO caller-supplied filesystem arguments: a caller cannot pass path, directory or project_path - Rust obtains the selection from the OS dialog itself. This does not weaken the renderer boundary, because a CAN-X project path is already the explicit input of the Runtime's GET /project/inspect contract. Rust must NOT validate that the selection is a CAN-X project: no reading project.json, no opening project.db, no schema check, no project-identity check, no copy of ProjectService logic. Project authority stays with the Python Runtime ProjectService; this bridge owns only the user filesystem selection. Errors are typed, static and bounded, and never echo the selected path. Reuse the existing tauri_plugin_dialog directory picker; add no dependency and do not modify Cargo.toml.
tasks.scope: The new Rust project-directory bridge module, its tests, the lib.rs command registration, and the DBC bridge's registered-command-surface regression test that the new registration invalidates.
non_goals: Any project validation, project identity check or ProjectService logic in Rust
Reading project.json, opening project.db or checking a schema from Rust
Any new crate dependency, any Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock change
Any renderer capability change, any TypeScript change and any Runtime change
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one new command is registered, named select_project_directory, and its only argument is the Tauri-injected AppHandle - no caller-supplied filesystem argument exists

The registered command surface regression in dbc_file_bridge/tests.rs is updated to the new reviewed surface AND its parameter scan is extended to project_directory_bridge.rs with its inspected-command count raised accordingly - the invariant is preserved, not weakened
Cancel resolves to Ok(None) and selection resolves to Ok(Some(directory path)); the bridge performs no project validation of the selection
Every failure is a declared typed code with static message text, and no published payload or error contains the selected directory path
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked all pass

tasks.title: Desktop project directory bridge and project-open orchestration
tasks.objective: Two connected pieces, both in the renderer. (A) A typed desktop bridge over the native select_project_directory command: selectProjectDirectory(): Promise<string | null>, invoked with no caller arguments, resolving null when the user cancelled and the selected project directory string otherwise; a native structured rejection becomes a typed bridge error and a malformed successful IPC payload is a contract error. The bridge reads no project.json, validates nothing, never calls a filesystem API directly and creates no global project state. (B) A pure project-open orchestration that composes the selection boundary with a project inspection boundary WITHOUT importing the Runtime client's implementation details, so it stays parallel-safe: it takes selectDirectory and inspectProject as injected functions (dependency injection or a structural function type) and the project read model as a generic / type-only seam, never as a duplicated copy of the Runtime project schema. Flow: selectProjectDirectory() -> null means cancelled and ends the function before any inspection call; otherwise the selected path is forwarded verbatim to inspectProject, and the outcome is an opened { projectPath, project } discriminated union. No path normalisation, no global current project, no persistent state, no DBC coupling and no error translation: a selection error and an inspection error both propagate exactly as thrown.
tasks.scope: The new TypeScript desktop directory bridge and the new project-open orchestration module, each with its vitest suite.
non_goals: Any Rust change - the native command is V0.3-12-B's surface and is consumed here only as a string
Importing or re-implementing the Runtime project client; the inspection boundary is injected
Any project picker UI, recent-projects list, project mutation or global current-project state
Duplicating the Runtime project read-model schema as a second authority
acceptance_criteria: The TypeScript bridge invokes the command named select_project_directory with no arguments, resolving null on cancel and the selected path on success
The bridge sorts a native rejection into a typed bridge error and a malformed successful IPC payload into a contract error; a bridge that is unavailable is reported as its own code
openProjectFromNativeDialog(selectDirectory, inspectProject) returns { status: 'cancelled' } without calling inspectProject when the selection is null
A selected path is forwarded to inspectProject exactly as returned - character for character - and one selection produces exactly one inspection call
An opened outcome carries { projectPath, project } with the read model typed structurally / generically, and a selection failure or an inspection failure propagates unchanged
No module-level mutable state: two sequential calls never share a project
